name: T1a
description: Haplogroup T1a is a subclade of T1, one of the two main branches of mtDNA haplogroup T. T1a is found throughout the Near East, East Africa, and at lower frequencies across Europe. It is particularly common in populations of the Arabian Peninsula, the Horn of Africa, and among Ashkenazi Jews. T1a appears to have experienced significant demographic expansion in the Near East during the Neolithic and subsequently spread through the movements of Semitic-speaking peoples and later with the Arab expansion of the Islamic period.
interestingFact: T1a is one of the four major mtDNA haplogroups (along with K1a1b1a, N1b, and X2e) that together account for the majority of Ashkenazi Jewish maternal lineages, pointing to a common female ancestral pool of Near Eastern origin for this population.

statistics.modernFrequency: ~1-2% globally; higher in Near East and East Africa
